provisioning.apply.what: type the current settings into the nodes that are already running, which is the difference between changing what a future run does and changing what this one is doing
provisioning.apply.answers: `nodes` counts the ones that had firmware up and were typed at; a node not running is passed over rather than refused, so a count below the size of the network is normal on a mesh that is still coming up. The commands are queued at each node's serial input, so the clock has to move before the firmware acts on them. A node whose console will not take a line ends the whole call with an error naming it, leaving the nodes after it untouched.

example.what: push changed settings into a mesh that is up

provisioning.get.what: read the switches every node is told at boot, which is what decides whether a mesh comes up named, positioned and in the same conversation as the rest
provisioning.get.answers: The settings themselves, unwrapped. A zero or an empty string is not a value sent to the firmware but a firmware default left alone, and `path_hash_mode` and `comp_path_hash_mode` say the same thing with -1.

example.what: read what the next start will send

provisioning.set.what: change what a future run tells its nodes, a switch at a time, leaving every setting not named where it was

params.name: set_name
params.what: send each node its scenario name; absent leaves it alone, and off leaves a node reporting as its board type

params.name: set_position
params.what: send each node its latitude and longitude; absent leaves it alone, and off leaves a node advertising no position

params.name: set_clock
params.what: set every node to the run's own epoch; absent leaves it alone, and off leaves clocks that reject traffic as replays

params.name: region_from_area
params.what: define a transport region named after the study area; absent leaves it alone

params.name: default_scope
params.what: make that region the one nodes originate under; absent leaves it alone, and off leaves them relaying but never originating

params.name: advert_hops
params.what: how far an advert may flood; absent leaves it alone and zero says nothing to the firmware

params.name: advert_minutes
params.what: how often a node says it is there; absent leaves it alone, zero means never, and anything outside 60 to 240 is clamped into that range because the firmware refuses the rest

params.name: stagger_ms
params.what: milliseconds between node starts; absent leaves it alone

params.name: flood_max_advert
params.what: how far an advert is relayed; absent leaves it alone and zero leaves the firmware's own limit

params.name: path_hash_mode
params.what: the repeaters' path-hash mode; absent leaves it alone and negative says nothing to the firmware

params.name: comp_path_hash_mode
params.what: the companions' own, which is a different question from the repeaters'; absent leaves it alone and negative falls back to path_hash_mode

params.name: loop_detect
params.what: the firmware's loop-detect setting, sent only to nodes that transmit; absent or empty leaves it alone

params.name: cad
params.what: the firmware's CAD mode, sent only to nodes that transmit; absent or empty leaves it alone

params.name: extra
params.what: further console lines, one per line, sent after the rest and unchecked; absent or empty leaves it alone

provisioning.set.answers: Every setting comes back, the same shape as `provisioning.get`, so one call both changes and reads. Nothing reaches a node that is already running: this is what the next start sends, and `provisioning.apply` is what changes a mesh that is up.

example.what: make the mesh advertise, and let adverts cross a country
